rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatt denotes going beyond measure and departing from truth; invoking a deity entails confessing its divinity, so this hypothetical claim would be outrageous injustice.
rows.anchor: جاوز القدر والحد وتباعد عن الحق

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Calling them our people admits the youths once shared their community's error, before God guided them to knowledge and freed them from desire and worldly worship.
rows.anchor: كنا من جملتهم وبالضلالة في زمرتهم فأنعم الله علينا بالهداية والمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative هؤلاء belittles the idolaters, and قومنا is an explanatory apposition; اتخذوا reports their ignorant worship of idols.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير باسم إشارة تحقير لهم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Here اتخذوا can mean either that they made the idols themselves or that they turned them into deities.
rows.anchor: اتخذوا هنا يحتمل أن يكون بمعنى عملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths demand clear proof for the idols' divinity; there is no revealed, transmitted, necessary, or rational proof, so unsupported religious claims are rejected.
rows.anchor: لم يتمسكوا في صحة عبادتها ببرهان سماوي من جهة الوحي والسمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge both rebukes and incapacitates idolaters, since producing proof for worship of idols is impossible.
rows.anchor: والآية إنكار وتعجيز وتبكيت لأن الإتيان بالسلطان على عبادة الأوثان محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating a partner with God is the greatest injustice and therefore merits the greatest punishment.
rows.anchor: أظلم من كل ظالم وعذابه أعظم من كل عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths' feared return to the persecutors' religion is inwardly a return to worship of the idols of desire and worldly passions and adornments.
rows.anchor: وهي عبادة أصنام الهوى وطواغيت شهوات الدنيا وزينتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For bodily, religious, moral, and reputational safety, one should withdraw from people into solitude like the cave youths; social mixing harms temperament and ends in conformity with people of desire.
rows.anchor: فليجدها في الوحدة والاعتزال عن الناس والإيواء إلى كهف البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three reports belong to disputants in the Prophet's era among scripturalists and Muslims, but the source does not assign every statement to every group.
rows.anchor: للخائضين في قصتهم في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أهل الكتاب والمسلمين

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: The Jews say the sleepers were three, with the dog making a fourth.
rows.anchor: أي : سيقول اليهود هم أي : أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: النصارى
rows.claim: The Christians say five sleepers and a sixth dog, but this is conjecture about the unseen; rajman can be circumstantial or a cognate accusative.
rows.anchor: أي : النصارى وإنما لم يجىء بالسين اكتفاء بعطفه

rows.speaker: المسلمون
rows.claim: The Muslims say seven sleepers and their dog as a conclusion received through revelation, not a conjecture like the preceding claims.
rows.anchor: القائلون المسلمون بطرق التلقن من هذا الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added waw in the seven-count formulation and its distinct wording convey a firmer relation and show it is guided by revelation rather than guesswork.
rows.anchor: وتغيير سبكه بزيادة الواو المفيدة لزيادة وكادة النسبة

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: My Lord knows best means stronger and more complete knowledge, since certainty has degrees; the comparison is not with the first two groups, who have no share in knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي أي : أقوى علما وأزيد في الكيفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a few know the sleepers' number, having been guided to use the relevant indications as evidence.
rows.anchor: ما يعلمهم عدتهم إلا قليل من الناس قد وفقهم الله للاستشهاد بتلك الشواهد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the waw as closing the count: there is no further number after seven, and the dog is eighth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما حين وقعت الواو وانقطعت العدة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali names six companions of the king and a seventh shepherd who joined their flight; the shepherd's name has variant forms.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنهم سبعة نفر أسماؤهم يمليخا ومكشليينا

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says the shepherd's name is more correctly Martush.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : الأصح أنه مرطوش

rows.speaker: النيسابوري عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed through Ibn Abbas recommends writing the sleepers' names for protection, healing, safe travel, childbirth, crops, wealth, and access to rulers.
rows.anchor: قال النيسابوري عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن أسماء أصحاب الكهف تصلح للطلب والهرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the first two counts are ignorant, avoid deep dispute; state the Quranic account without humiliating them and do not consult people who lack knowledge.
rows.anchor: إذ قد عرفت جهل أصحاب القولين الأولين فلا تجادلهم

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: One esoteric interpretation makes the seven sleepers the seven abdal sustaining the world's seven climes, their cave a retreat, and their dog the animal soul.
rows.anchor: بعض كويند اين قصه نمود از أحوال بدلاء سبعة است

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers join works of the heart to works of the bodily limbs; صالحات became a conventional noun for deeds approved by religious law.
rows.anchor: جمعوا بين عمل القلب وعمل الأركان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording identifies good action as the basis of earned reward, while knowledge brings elevation in degrees, honor, and rank.
rows.anchor: أن الأجر إنما يستحق بالعمل دون العلم إذ به يستحق ارتفاع الدرجات

rows.speaker: حديث قدسي
rows.claim: A sacred report distinguishes entry into Paradise by God's grace from allocation of its ranks according to deeds.
rows.anchor: ادخلوا الجنة بفضلي واقتسموها بأعمالكم

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage a Bedouin asked about the verse; the Prophet identified Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali beside him and said it was revealed about them, as al-Suhayli records.
rows.anchor: وعن البراء بن عازب رضي الله عنه قال : قام أعرابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adn can mean a place of residence or the proper name of Paradise's central, most honored region; the plural gardens may mean the two gardens in the cited passage or an individual garden for each person.
rows.anchor: الإقامة فيجوز أن يكون المعنى أولئك لهم جنات إقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivers are of water, milk, wine, and honey; flowing water makes a garden especially choice.
rows.anchor: الأربعة من الخمر واللبن والعسل والماء العذب

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi paraphrases the promise as their being adorned in those gardens.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (يرايه بسته شوند دران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first min introduces bracelets and the second explains their material; the indefinite wording magnifies their beauty.
rows.anchor: وتنكيرها لتعظيم حسنها وتبعيده من الإحالة به

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-Ulum says the indefinite bracelets also suggest abundance and magnificence.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" وتنكير أساور للتكثير

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says each person wears three bracelets, of gold, silver, and pearl or ruby, either in succession or together.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير يحلى كل واحد منهم ثلاثة أساور

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some spiritual masters read gold bracelets as realities of essential unity and silver as the luminous attributes, linked to the silver bracelets in 76:21.
rows.anchor: فالذهبيات هي الذاتيات والفضيات هي الصفات النوريات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is fine silk and istabraq thick silk; pairing both kinds signals delight to the soul and eye, and istabraq is a Persian loan rather than a derivation from barq.
rows.anchor: ما رق من الديباج وما غلظ منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adornment is passive because God or angels confer it as an added honor, while clothing is actively attributed to its wearers as something they put on themselves.
rows.anchor: في الحلي يحلون على فعل ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People dress themselves, even if kings, while others ordinarily adorn them; the passive adornment wording therefore conveys honor and gracious treatment.
rows.anchor: لباس الستر يلبسه المرء بنفسه ولو كان سلطانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An arika is a bed within a curtained bridal alcove, not a bare bed; reclining is the posture of the prosperous and royal.
rows.anchor: وهي السرير في الحجال ولا يسمى السرير وحده أريكة

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata reads the couches inwardly as intimacy in sacred gardens and fields of mercy, where the people of union witness their Lord in every state.
rows.anchor: متكئين على أرائك الإنس في رياض القدس وميادين الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good reward is the gardens and their delights; the resting place is a couch and a home for repose.
rows.anchor: والثواب جزاء الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preparation for Paradise requires righteous deeds done for God, including fasting, prayer, and other good works.
rows.anchor: فالصالحات من الأعمال من الأسباب المعدة لها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Deeds that lead to the gardens are bodily worship done with sound intention and in accordance with the law; deeds that lead to God are inner truthfulness, sincerity, detachment, wholehearted turning, and following a perfected guide.
rows.anchor: ومنها أعمال تصلح للسير إلى الله تعالى وهي الطاعات القلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not rely on wishes: one who sows barley cannot harvest wheat; an anecdote mocks a servant who expected wheat after planting barley and a master who disobeys God while expecting mercy.
rows.anchor: فإن من زرع الشعير لا يحصد حنطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable is directed to unbelievers immersed in blessings and believers enduring poverty, and concerns two men, perhaps brothers from Israel.
rows.anchor: وبين للكافرين المتقلبين في نعم الله والمؤمنين المكابدين لمشاق الفقر

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn identifies the two as sons of a king among the Israelites.
rows.anchor: قال في الجلالين : يريد ابني ملك كان في بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan infers from the term companion that the two men were not brothers.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان ويظهر من قوله : {فقال لصاحبه} أنه ليس أخاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Abu Hayyan's inference: a brother can be called a companion, and the later scene of a man taking his brother through the garden supports their being siblings.
rows.anchor: التعبير عنهما برجلين يصحح إطلاق الصاحب على الأخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account names the believing brother Yahuda and the unbeliever Qutrus; after inheriting eight thousand dinars, the believer gave his half away for heavenly land, a home, spouses, and servants, then became poor and was refused help.
rows.anchor: كان أحد الأخوين مؤمنا واسمه يهودا والآخر كافرا واسمه قطروس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two grape gardens are vineyards by metonymy or an ellipsis for grape trees; palms surround them and crops between them make a well ordered, productive whole.
rows.anchor: ليكون كل منهما جامعا للأقوات والفواكه متواصل العمارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both gardens yielded ripe fruit without losing any, unlike orchards whose yield often falls in a year or whose trees bear intermittently.
rows.anchor: لم تنقض من أكلها {شياا} كما يعهد في سائر البساتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The river is mentioned after fruit despite irrigation's normal priority to show both blessings independently complete the gardens; it hints that fruit can be given without watering, as in 24:35.
rows.anchor: للإيذان باستقلال كل من إيتاء الأكل وتفجير النهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ثمر includes kinds of wealth beyond the gardens; explicitly mentioning produce signals his abundant harvest and other assets.
rows.anchor: وذكرها وإن كانت الجنة لا تخلو عنها إيذان بكثرة الحاصل له

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says he had every kind of fruit, including grapes, dates, and others, named because these were most prominent.
rows.anchor: واختصاص آنها بذكر غالبيت بوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion is the believing brother; يحاوره means conversing and answering back, which explains the description of their exchange.
rows.anchor: يكلمه ويراجعه الكلام من حار إذا رجع

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan defines wealth broadly as all owned goods and property, while al-mal al-ayn is specifically coined money.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن الحسن رحمه الله : المال كله ما يتملكه الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafar means male helpers, sons, or retinue, conventionally three to ten men and not more.
rows.anchor: والنفر بفتحتين من الثلاثة إلى العشرة من الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sees a difficulty if the comparative is literal: two actual brothers inherited equal shares, so the believer should not have had no wealth while the unbeliever had more; he leaves the answer unresolved.
rows.anchor: لاح لي ههنا إشكال وهو أنه إن حمل أفعل على حقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutrus enters one garden while showing it off to his brother; the gardens are treated as one because they adjoin or because one enters them one at a time.
rows.anchor: صاحب الجنتين وهو قطروس {جنته} بصاحبه يطوف به فيها

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Sheikh explains the singular garden as referring to the garden or orchard as a whole.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ : افردها إرادة للروضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wrongs himself through vanity in his wealth and disbelief in the Creator and return, a particularly grave injustice.
rows.anchor: يعجب بماله وكفره بالمبدأ والمعاد وهو أقبح الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ظن is often borrowed for knowledge or near-certainty; perish means disappear, and أبدا means the long duration of his life rather than literal eternity, reflecting long hope and heedlessness.
rows.anchor: والمراد هنا المكث الطويل وهو مدة حياته لا الدوام المؤبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour means the time of resurrection; his hypothetical return to God does not prove recognition of God, since awareness can coexist with idolatry.
rows.anchor: فليس فيه دلالة على أنه كان عارفا بربه مع أن العرفان لا ينافي الإشراك

rows.speaker: البرهان
rows.claim: Al-Burhan explains the wording difference from 41:50: returning from his beloved garden is framed as an unwanted being sent back, while that context has no sign of aversion and uses a different verb.
rows.anchor: ولما كان في الكهف تقديره ولئن رددت عن جنتي هذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His boast of finding something better rests on the false belief that worldly favor reflects inherent worth and will follow him; he mistakes divine respite for gradual entrapment.
rows.anchor: اعتقاد أنه تعالى إنما أولاه في الدنيا لاستحقاقه الذاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claiming that a generous God will reward someone who defies His commands is delusion, as the cited warning links arrogance about divine generosity to the fate of sinners.
rows.anchor: كما قال : يا اأيها الانسان ما غرك بربك الكريم}

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The circumstantial phrase about their dialogue alerts the listener that the ensuing speech is important to the exchange.
rows.anchor: وفائدة هذه الجملة الحالية التنبيه من الأمر الأول على أن ما يتلوه كلام معتنى بشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer's question treats denial of resurrection as doubt in God's attributes and power; the man derives through Adam from dust, then from his mother's sperm, and is shaped upright as an adult male.
rows.anchor: أي : من مني في رحم أمك ثانيا وهي مادتك القريبة

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon says rajul is the familiar word for a man, or specifically a male who has reached puberty and grown up.
rows.anchor: قال في "القاموس" الرجل بضم الجيم وسكونها معروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakinna ana contracts by dropping the hamza, with disagreement about vowel transfer; most readers keep its alif only at pause, while Ibn Amir also keeps it in connection.
rows.anchor: أصله لكن أنا فحذفت الهمزة بنقل حركتها إلى نون لكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause Allah is my Lord is the predicate of the pronoun of the matter, and the whole clause predicates ana; لكن contrasts his belief with his brother's disbelief.
rows.anchor: وهو ضمير الشأن مبتدأ خبره الله ربي وتلك الجملة خبر أنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His refusal to associate anyone with his Lord indicates that the brother's unbelief took the form of associating partners.
rows.anchor: فيه إيذان بأن كفره كان بطريق الإشراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer hopes his faith will bring him a better garden in the enduring afterlife than the other's perishable worldly garden.
rows.anchor: خيرا من جنتك} هذه في الآخرة بسبب إيماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He predicts ruin for the ungrateful man because ingratitude leads to loss and self-admiration brings ruin, in keeping with the rule that God does not change a people until they change themselves.
rows.anchor: لعلمه بأن الكفران مؤد إلى الخسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A heavenly hesab may be hail, lightning, or fire; the garden would become slippery, smooth ground after its plants and trees are removed.
rows.anchor: حسبانا من السمآء} عذابا يرميها

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi allows zalqan to evoke a shaved head: the garden would be bare of vegetation like a shaven scalp.
rows.anchor: وجوز القرطبي أن تكون زلقا من زلق رأسه أي : حلقه

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says faith and obedience benefit only when desired as faith and obedience, not merely to gain reward or avoid punishment.
rows.anchor: الرغبة في الإيمان والطاعة لا تنفع إلا إذا كانت تلك الرغبة رغبة لكونه إيمانا وطاعة

rows.speaker: مولانا
rows.claim: The Mathnawi portrays remorse born only of suffering as worthless once the suffering disappears, and invokes the warning that people would relapse if returned.
rows.anchor: ميكند او توبة ور خرد بانك لو ردوا لعادوا ميزند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No group could avert the garden's destruction or replace it, because God alone could do so but withheld help from the man who deserved abandonment through unbelief and disobedience.
rows.anchor: فإنه القادر وحده على نصره بذلك لا غير لكنه لا ينصره لاستحقاقه الخذلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that moment all support belongs to God alone; alternatively, He is the best reward and end for His friends, whom He aids over unbelievers and vindicates as in the garden owner's fate.
rows.anchor: ينصر فيها أولياءه المؤمنين على الكفرة وينتقم لهم

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: The good end includes worldly outcomes as well as the final outcome.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي وعقبى يشمل العاقبة الدنيوية أيضا

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn glosses the best reward as better than the reward hoped for from others, and obedience to God as having the better outcome.
rows.anchor: أفضل ثوابا ممن يرجى ثوابه وعاقبة طاعته خير من عاقبة طاعة غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will remove mountains from their places and move them through the air intact or reduce them to dispersed dust, a warning to idolaters about the terrors of that Day.
rows.anchor: نقلعها من أماكنها وتسير في الجو على هيآتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth will be exposed with no mountain, tree, or plant to cover it, and everyone, believer and unbeliever, will be gathered with no one left beneath it.
rows.anchor: ظاهرة ليس عليها ما يسترها من جبل ولا شجر ولا نبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathered are displayed in ranks before God's judgment like troops before a ruler, not to identify them; a singular صف stands for rows of people.
rows.anchor: {صفا} مفرد منزل منزلة الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They come as first created: barefoot and naked, without possessions or children.
rows.anchor: حفاة عراة لا شيء من المال والولد

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha asked the Prophet how people, including women, would be gathered; he said barefoot and naked, and that the terror would leave them no thought of looking at one another.
rows.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها قلت : يا رسول الله كيف يحشر الناس

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: An inward reading divides the assembly into five rows: prophets, saints, believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites.
rows.anchor: صف من الأنيباء ، وصف من الأولياء ، وصف من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke recalls the disbelievers' false claim that no appointment would ever be made for resurrection and its consequences; بل shifts the account to censure.
rows.anchor: زعمتم في الدنيا أنه لن نجعل لكم أبدا وقتا ننجز فيه

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A report says Umar was seen twelve years after his death still undergoing reckoning over a kid goat injured at a broken bridge, though he had neither harmed it nor repaired the bridge; he says releasing a sparrow brought forgiveness.
rows.anchor: روي أن عمر رضي الله عنه رؤى بعد موته بثنتي عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The placement of the record follows the assembly and includes deedsheets in the right or left hands or in the balance; criminals fear their sins being exposed to all present.
rows.anchor: وضع صحف الأعمال في إيمان أصحابها وشمائلها أو في الميزان

rows.speaker: مولانا
rows.claim: The cited Persian poem pictures records of sin and disobedience as heavy evidence that keeps the wrongdoer's record from the right hand.
rows.anchor: جمله فسق ومعصيت بد يكسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call for their own destruction, personifying doom and begging it to arrive so they need not face the horror they have encountered.
rows.anchor: منادين لهلكتهم التي هلكوا بها من بين الهلكات

rows.speaker: البقاعي
rows.claim: Al-Biqai says the unusual writing of the lām hints that terror and distress leave them able to utter only part of the word; the book contains and records every slip.
rows.anchor: رسم لام الجر وحده إشارة إلى أنهم صاروا من قوة الرعب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas classifies a smile as a minor sin and loud laughter as a major one.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : الصغيرة التبسم والكبيرة القهقهة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr calls touching a minor sin and illicit sex a major one.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير : الصغيرة المسيس والكبيرة الزنا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading calls any desire-driven use of something minor, even in devotional conversation, while using the world out of love is major even if lawful, since worldly love heads every sin.
rows.anchor: الكبيرة التصرف في الدنيا على حبها وإن كان من حلالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two prophetic reports warn against belittled sins: people gather small sticks until they can cook, and such sins may appear like mountains on Judgment Day; charity is named as expiation.
rows.anchor: إياكم ومحقرات الذنوب فإن محقرات الذنوب كمثل قوم نزلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book contains either the worldly acts themselves or their recompense, set down in the record.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا من السيآت أو جزاء ما عملوا

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, good acts are inscribed in the heart's pages and bad acts in the self's pages, though the two can also appear oppositely on spiritual pages.
rows.anchor: كتبوا صالح أعمالهم بقلم أفعالهم في صحائف قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God neither records sins a person did not commit nor increases punishment beyond the corresponding deed, manifesting the justice of the primordial Pen.
rows.anchor: أو يزيد في عقابه الملائم لعمله

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A soul's prevailing light leads to Paradise and degrees of nearness; prevailing darkness dooms it, though divine attraction may transform sins into good and bring it into true light.
rows.anchor: فإن كان النور غالبا على صفحة روحه فهو من أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam's prostration was honor and greeting, not worship, and was a former religious law later replaced by greeting with peace.
rows.anchor: سجود تحية وتكريم لا سجود عبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All commanded angels prostrated, while the high spirits did not because they were not included in the command.
rows.anchor: الملائكة العالون لأنهم لم يؤمروا بالسجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis was a jinn created from fire, not an angel; the apparent connected exception is valid because he was commanded along with the angels.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن من الملائكة وإنما صح الاستثناء المتصل لأنه أمر بالسجود معهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternative explanations make Iblis the first jinn, a remnant of a pre-Adam people called jinn, or a survivor of an earlier disobedient creation destroyed by fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه كان بقايا قوم يقال لهم الجن

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi gives Iblis's earlier names as Azazil in Syriac and al-Harith in Arabic; after disobedience he was called Iblis for despairing of mercy.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : كان اسمه عزازيل بالسريانية وبالعربية الحارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fusuq means leaving obedience; the command can mean God's order or the commanded prostration, and Iblis's being a jinn explains his capacity to disobey, unlike angels.
rows.anchor: كونه من الجن سبب فسقه ولو كان ملكا لم يفسق عن أمر ربه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says Iblis cast off the collar of imitation; a trial reveals the accepted from the rejected, like fire exposing what only resembles musk.
rows.anchor: وخلع قلادة التقليد عن عنقه ليعلم أن الأصيل لا يخطىء

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Hafiz's verse welcomes the test that exposes a liar's shame.
rows.anchor: فلما امتحنا بالنار تبين المقبول من المردود والمبغوض من المودود ، وقال الحافظ قدس سره :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes and marvels at people taking Iblis as an ally after his rebellion; his offspring may figuratively mean his followers.
rows.anchor: أي : عقيب عملكم يا بني آدم بصدور الفسق عن إبليس

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says ذرية may mean followers figuratively, and most hold that they are not his literal offspring.
rows.anchor: كويند بمعنى اتباع وتسميه ايشان بذريت ازقبيل مجاز بود

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: The lexicon says dara'a means to create or increase, and dhurriyya names the descendants of humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: ذرأ كجعل خلق والشيء كثره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking Iblis and his offspring as allies means replacing obedience to God with obedience to them, even though they are enemies; it is a wretched substitute.
rows.anchor: فتستبدلونهم بي فتطيعونهم بدل طاعتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not bring Iblis and his progeny to witness creation or consult them as helpers, since the heavens and earth were created before them; this denies that they share divinity or know the unseen.
rows.anchor: ما أحضرت إبليس وذريته {خلق السماوات والارض} لاعتضد بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nor did God make some of them witness the creation of others; the phrasing is compared with the command not to kill yourselves in 4:29.
rows.anchor: كقوله تعالى : {ولا تقتلوا أنفسكم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them misleaders rather than using a pronoun condemns their work, while عضدا means helpers or supporters.
rows.anchor: فوضع المظهر موضع المضمر ذما لهم وتسجيلا عليهم بالإضلال

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines عضد as a supporter or helper.
rows.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : العضد الناصر والمعين

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib distinguishes angels, who have no sex, offspring, food, or drink, from jinn, who are male and female, reproduce, and die; devils reproduce but are said to remain alive in the world.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب الملائكة ليسوا بذكور ولا إناث ولا يتوالدون

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli and other transmitters give lore that Iblis produces eggs and name offspring including Aqbass and Balzun, the latter assigned to markets; al-Naqqash says thirty eggs produced different devil kinds.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام السهيلي في كتاب "التعريف والاعلام" سمي من ولد إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers that God Himself address the unbelievers on Judgment Day, though some say angels speak; God will appear to people in forms according to their beliefs, and reproachful speech is plausible after speaking to cursed Iblis.
rows.anchor: الأظهر هو الأول لأنه قد ثبت أن الله تعالى يتجلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the command to call the alleged partners is delivered by angels.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : يقول على ألسنة الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls them His partners sarcastically, to shame their claim that they would intercede, and means everything worshipped besides Him.
rows.anchor: أضافهم إليه على زعمهم تهكما بهم وتقريعا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their call for aid is described elsewhere as followers asking their supposed gods for relief.
rows.anchor: ذكر كيفية دعوتهم في آية أخرى {إنا كنا لكم تبعا فهل أنتم مغنون عنا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partners do not rescue or benefit them, though this does not rule out a formal spoken reply; obedience matters before death, since their afterlife obedience to the command to call gains nothing.
rows.anchor: أي : لم يدفعوا عنهم ضرا ولا أوصلوا إليهم نفعا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra reads the worldly bond between worshippers and worshipped as becoming their destruction in the afterlife; the word between can mean that bond, as in 6:94.
rows.anchor: قال الفرآء : {وجعلنا} تواصلكم في الدنيا هلاكا في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawbiq may be the place or shared cause of destruction, such as Hell or an enmity as severe as destruction.
rows.anchor: وهو النار أو عداوة هي في الشدة نفس الهلاك

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines mawbiq as a place of destruction, a valley in Hell, or anything separating two things.
rows.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : الموبق كمجلس المهلك وواد في جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a separating barrier between worshippers and the worshipped, preventing intercession by angels, Jesus, or Ezra without precluding their being together; sharing the fire applies to those destined to enter it.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير الظاهر أن المعنى على الثالث أي : جعلنا بينهم

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi describes the polytheists as seeing Hell when they are driven to it.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (وبه بيند مشركان آتش دوزخ را

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ظن means certainty, and falling into the fire is called contact or mixture because the contact is so complete.
rows.anchor: فأيقنوا {أنهم مواقعوها} مخالطوها واقعون فيها

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says they likely see Hell from afar but immediately know they will fall into it from its furious roaring; it is five hundred years away, as 25:12 says.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام : والأقرب أنهم يرون النار من بعيد فيظنون أنهم مواقعوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A maṣrif is a turning away or a place of escape, but the fire surrounds them on every side.
rows.anchor: انصرافا أو مكانا ينصرفون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears that He has repeated and varied many forms and arrangements for people's benefit, including the two-gardens parable, worldly-life examples, and calls to faith.
rows.anchor: أقسم قسما لقد كررنا وأدرنا على وجوه كثيرة من النظم

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says people need examples from past stories to learn and proofs of divine power to deepen insight.
rows.anchor: ازهر مثل بران محتاجند از قصص كذشته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are more argumentative than other creatures capable of dispute; here the term means fierce argument for falsehood, though argument itself need not be false, and its root suggests twisting against an opponent.
rows.anchor: وإلا فالجدل لا يلزم أن يكون بالباطل

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: A prophetic report transmitted by Abu Umama says a people do not stray after guidance except that they are given disputation; it is cited from Abu al-Layth's commentary.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "ما ضل قوم بعد هدى كانوا عليه إلا أوتوا الجدل" رواه أبو أمامة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says argument blocks people's own path: they dispute prophecy, scripture, legal and ambiguous passages, abrogation, interpretation, revelation occasions, readings, and scripture's createdness, never reaching action, obedience, or communion.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" من طبيعة الإنسان المجادلة والمخاصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wise person should work on himself and leave quarrels, since argument divides people and is a trait of predatory nature; if even a person who is right must leave it, the case is worse for a false disputant.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يشتغل بنفسه ويترك المراء والجدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says faith is not complete until one gives up contentious argument even when right; believers should pass by idle talk graciously and answer the ignorant with peace.
rows.anchor: لا يستكمل عبد حقيقة الإيمان حتى يدع المراء وإن كان محقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccans were held back from faith and seeking forgiveness only by waiting for the destruction that befell earlier peoples or for visible kinds of punishment.
rows.anchor: إلا} انتظار {أن تأتيهم سنة الاولين}

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn identifies the punishment as the killing at Badr.
rows.anchor: قال في "الجلالين" يعني القتل يوم بدر

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: A question asks why one of two punishments was promised but not inflicted on every unbeliever; the answer is that the threat applied if all refused faith, whereas most believed at the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: الجواب إنما وعدهم بذلك إن تركوا الإيمان كلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers bring believers and obedient people good news of reward and degrees, and warn unbelievers and sinners of punishment; reason alone cannot fully discern either path, so sending messengers is divine mercy.
rows.anchor: فكان من لطف الله ورحمته أن أرسل الرسل لبيان ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars who serve like the prophets of Israel are also a mercy: they dispel doubts and guide seekers toward full understanding and spiritual progress.
rows.anchor: إذ ببيانهم يضمحل ظلم الشبه وينحل عقد الشكوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers argue falsely that prophets are merely human and demand more signs despite miracles, trying to dislodge truth; the verb evokes slipping from a foothold.
rows.anchor: حيث يقولون : ما أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا ولو شاء الله لأنزل ملائكة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says monotheists' proofs cannot be dislodged by specious arguments, asking how what Abraham raised could be put down by Abrahah.
rows.anchor: حجج الموحدين لا تدحض بشبه المشبه

rows.speaker: مولانا
rows.claim: The Mathnawi compares God's light to a candle: one who blows against it only burns himself while the flame remains.
rows.anchor: هركه بر شمع خدا آرد فو شمع كى ميرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers treated signs of God's oneness and power and the warnings they received as objects of mockery.
rows.anchor: الدالة على الوحدة والقدرة ونحوهما {ومآ أنذروا} خوفوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worst wrongdoer turns away from Quranic admonition and forgets his own prior sins and their consequences; hands stand for the many deeds people do, including inner acts.
rows.anchor: لما كان الإنسان يباشر أكثر أعماله بيديه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the most unjust is one who sees the signs but draws no lesson, turns from good, and follows rather than avoids the sites of evil.
rows.anchor: أحق الناس تسمية بالظلم من يرى الآيات فلا يعتبر بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coverings on hearts explain neglect and forgetfulness, preventing comprehension, while the weight in ears prevents listening; people of idle talk do not heed Quran.
rows.anchor: إهمالهم كما في "تفسير الشيخ" {على قلوبهم أكنة}

rows.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
rows.claim: Al-Kamal al-Khujandi's verse describes the heart recoiling from hearing the Quran and falsehood tiring of God's true speech.
rows.anchor: دل از شنيدن قرآن بكير درهمه وقت

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says this specifically concerns Meccan unbelievers whom God knew would never believe.
rows.anchor: مراد جمعي اند از كفار مكه كه علم حق بعدم ايمان ايشان متعلق بود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of no guidance lasts through the whole period of moral responsibility because their chosen turning away has made guidance impossible for them.
rows.anchor: فلن يكون منهم اهتداء البتة مدة التكليف كلها لأنه محال منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghafur is emphatic for covering deserved punishment by forgiving sins; rahma is beneficence, a further report of God's quality.
rows.anchor: البليغ في المغفرة وهي صيانة العبد عما استحقه من العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form of forgiveness, unlike mercy, reflects the abundance of sins: harms that can be withheld are unlimited, while acts of creation and benefit are finite; cleansing precedes adornment.
rows.anchor: وإيراد المغفرة على صيغة المبالغة دون الرحمة للتنبيه على كثرة الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God seized people for their sins, He could promptly punish them in this world; instead He gives respite until an appointed time, either Badr or Resurrection.
rows.anchor: {لعجل لهم العذاب} في الدنيا من غير إمهال لاستيجاب أعمالهم

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Sa'di al-Mufti prefers taking من دونه as apart from the punishment: if punishment itself is their only refuge, the impossibility of escape is stated especially forcefully.
rows.anchor: قال سعدي المفتي : هو أولى وفيه دلالة على أبلغ وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mawil is a rescuer or refuge; the phrase may also mean they find no shelter when the appointed time arrives.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى لن يجدوا عند حلول الموعد موئلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroyed towns are those of Aad, Thamud, and similar peoples; their wrongdoing resembles Meccan denial, shirk, and sins, and lamma may be causal or temporal over the period of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: قرى عاد وثمود وأضرابهما

rows.speaker: ابن عصفور
rows.claim: Ibn Asfour treats lamma as either a particle or a temporal expression used causally, not just the precise instant a sin occurred.
rows.anchor: ولما إما حرف كما قال ابن عصفور وإما ظرف استعمل للتعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God set an appointed time for their destruction; mahlak denotes destruction, and the date cannot be delayed or escaped.
rows.anchor: الهلاك {موعدا} ممتدا لا يتأخرون عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh should learn from earlier peoples; the proverb says a fortunate person takes warning from another's fate.
rows.anchor: السعيد من وعظ بغيره

rows.speaker: رشيد الدين وطواط
rows.claim: Tuwat's verse praises the fortunate person who accepts good counsel and learns from admonitions given to others.
rows.anchor: نيكبخت آن كسى بودكه دلش آنه نيكو تراست بذيرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even when all means of guidance are present, people believe only through God's gracious attraction; spiritual seekers cannot arrive without the Beloved's pull.
rows.anchor: أسباب الهداية وإن اجتمعت بالكلية لا يهتدي بها الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance also comes through the sword, in keeping with reports that the Prophet was commanded to fight until people profess God's oneness and was the prophet of the sword and battle.
rows.anchor: فالاهتداء بهداية الله تعالى وبالسيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false see truth as false because their hearts are blind, whereas people of truth follow prophets and saints by God's light, obeying signs instead of mocking them.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن أهل الباطل يرون الحق باطلا والباطل حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly mercy encompasses believers and unbelievers through provision and respite, while mercy in the next life is for believers and punishment for unbelievers; unjust communities are destroyed for adding oppression to unbelief.
rows.anchor: رحمة الله تعالى في الدنيا تعم المؤمن والكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly reign may last despite unbelief but not oppression; the oppressed person's prayer has no barrier, explaining the description of Anushirwan as just despite his being a Magian, though shirk itself is great injustice.
rows.anchor: الملك يبقى مع الكفر ولا يبقى مع الظلم
